text:
jamal: Heads up — us-west1 scratch pool is hitting sustained IO saturation, GPUs are getting attach failures and provisioning is backing off. saw ~12% attach errors in the last 5m. anyone digging?

olivia: on it, pulling metrics now. is this localized to pool-a or across all scratchpools?

mira: I see heavy write amplif on nodes in pool-a (gnode-*-usw1), IOPS at 98th percentile. NVMe busy% is 95% on several hosts.

jamal: logs showed `err=EIO` during attach in k8s events. pods stuck in ContainerCreating.

alex: quick grep of janitor logs shows overlapping scrub and aggressive prefetching yesterday night. janitor ran full-window scrub at 03:10 UTC. Probably heated the drives.

ben: posting quick iostat snapshot from node-47: 

```
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
           4.21    0.00    2.03    73.45    0.00   20.31
Device            tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s    kB_read    kB_wrtn
nvme0n1         1456       10240       51200    6144000   30720000
```

mira: nvme-cli stats show heavy write queues and long io latency tails (p99 > 120ms).

olivia: are we seeing any SMART errors or remapped sector growth?

ben: no SMART CRCs, just rising media wear on a subset (beta batch of drives). wear % jumped 3% over last 48h on ~8 hosts.

sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1832 - us-west1 scratch IO saturation. Pager: on-call-sre.

jamal: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle janitor/garbage-collector jobs 2) move ephemeral GPU scheduling to fallback pool (us-west2) 3) temporarily prevent new batch jobs from landing on affected nodes via taint. Thoughts?

mira: I can throttle janitor scrubs per-pool (we added rate limit flags last quarter). Recommend cut to 10% of normal.

olivia: I'll start the taint on affected nodes to stop new pods from scheduling. command: `kubectl taint nodes gnode-47 ephemeral-io=hot:NoSchedule`

alex: also reduce fstrim frequency — trim is expensive at scale. config is in cloud-init on image; can flip to weekly from daily as a short-term.

ben: note: throttling scrubs reduces wear but increases stale-file backlog; may spike later. tradeoff vs immediate attach failures.

jamal: do it anyway, attach failures blocking prod. olivia please apply taint + drain low priority batch pods, mig jobs to fallback pool. mira flip janitor rate-limit. alex change fstrim schedule and push a canary.

olivia: starting drain on gnode-47..49 for low-pri workloads. will keep one GPU host for critical services.

mira: set janitor config: `--scrub-rate=0.1 --parallelism=2` for pool-a. pushing via configmap now.

alex: updated cloud-init fstrim cron from `@daily` to `@weekly` and queued a rolling image config. will roll canary to 3 hosts.

ben: started moving ephemeral scheduling for `batch-gpu` to us-west2 fallback by updating Provisioner label selector. will monitor cost impact.

jamal: cost note — fallback pool has higher egress/cross-region price. but short spike preferable to failed attaches. log that as temporary mitigation cost.

olivia: drains done for nodes 47-49 (low-pri). left critical pods on gnode-48. attach failures for new pods dropped to 1% in last 2m.

mira: NVMe busy% dropped to ~70% after throttles and drains. latency p99 down to 45ms.

jamal: awesome. next: schedule remediation sprint — identify beta drives cohort, run targeted replacements, and refine janitor scheduling windows to avoid peak provisioning hours.

alex: proposing follow-ups: 1) Replace 8 drives (owner: hw-team) 2) Add IO pressure alert at 85% busy% and auto-throttle janitor (owner: eng-infra) 3) Add probe to reject heavy scrubs during rolling GPU provisioning windows (owner: scheduler).

ben: I'll open a draft runbook change for auto-throttle and link to incident.

olivia: leaving taints in place for 1h, will remove if metrics stable.

jamal: assign owners and ETA: hw-team ticket in 2d, runbook PR today, alert config PR by EOD.

sre-bot: Incident #INC-2026-1832 updated: status=mitigated, notes="throttled scrubs, drained low-pri, moved batch to fallback"

mira: quick summary for postmortem: root cause = concentrated janitor scrub + a small cohort of higher-wear NVMe drives during peak GPU provisioning window causing IOPS saturation and attach failures. mitigation = immediate rate limit + scheduling changes + hardware replacement plan.

jamal: Thanks team. I'll own the follow-up doc and link the runbook changes. ping me if attach rates increase. :thumbsup:
